mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC rose in each of the last four weekly means (-36.9, -34.3, -33.3, -32.4), a monotone recovery trend of +4.5 points. This drift persists into the next 28 days, so the forward mean exceeds the trailing mean.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below -32.4, i.e. the prior monotone improvement fails to extend at all.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES of more than 5 points (-27.7 to -35.4) marks a newly imposed stay-at-home directive. Such directives cut discretionary retail trips, so RETAIL_REC declines over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its t-0w level of -32.4 within two weeks of the WORKPLACES drop exceeding 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM improved 4.0 points in the final week (-5.3 to -1.3), the largest single-week gain of any series. Household provisioning trips co-locate with retail errands, so this grocery normalization leads a near-term RETAIL_REC uptick.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed -32.4 in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week gain of 4 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-29.0 to -31.4) and WORKPLACES (-27.7 to -35.4) both fell in the final week. The joint contraction removes commute-linked retail and recreation trips, and their conjunction predicts a deeper RETAIL_REC decline than either series alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is flat or higher over the two weeks in which TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fall simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restriction regime, RESIDENTIAL above +10 signals a home-bound population. Its final-week jump to 11.6 from 10.3 precedes reduced out-of-home spending, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL stays above 11.0.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS fell 1.4 points in the final week (-56.6 to -58.0) and TRANSIT slipped 2.4 points over the same interval. Falling discretionary-outing proxies indicate suppressed trip generation, which pulls RETAIL_REC lower within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week in the week following a PARKS decline greater than 1 point.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week gain in RETAIL_REC decelerated across the window (+1.4, +1.0, +0.9) while GROCERY_PHARM accelerated, meaning discretionary recovery is stalling and provisioning is absorbing the trips. The forward mean should therefore not exceed the trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact: RETAIL_REC weekly deltas are +2.6, +1.0, +0.9 while GROCERY_PHARM delta is +4.0 in the final week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves by more than 2 points over the next 28 days, contradicting the observed deceleration.

mechanism_narrative: The snapshot sits two weeks before the late-November holiday shopping window. Seasonal gift and food purchasing lifts retail-and-recreation footfall through that window regardless of the restriction backdrop, raising the forward 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact: decision time point is 2020-11-15, inside the pre-holiday shopping ramp
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is below its last-28-day mean of -32.4 despite the holiday shopping window.
